answer: Seats are priced in water, not signatures. Each binds a living vine to a sap-flow probe reporting nightly, and pays only when its draw matches an auctioned allotment: one per vine, unsellable, drunk by the plant. At the dry-season nadir it must still clear a minimum flow, so a probe on dead wood reads zero and the seat lapses. Wallets sharing a vine fold into one; the ledger counts plants, not keys. A thousand sybil agents demand a thousand vines, a thousand metres of metered water, a thousand night readings: cost scales with headcount, emissions do not. The horizon of profit never arrives.
